Paṭṭhāna — Volume II Foreword by I.B. Horner p. 19

Foreword In p. viii 1969 the Pāḷi Text Society published important translations of two Abhidhamma works: Conditional Relations, being Voḷ I of the Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana text of Paṭṭhāna, and No. 37 in the Translation Series by U Nārada Mūla Paṭṭhāna Sayadaw; and The Book of Analysis, Vibhaṅga, translated also from the Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana edition by Paṭhamakyaw Ashin Thiṭṭila, No. 39 in the Translation Serieṣ A third, and revised, edition of Mrs Rhys David’s translation of Dhammasaṅgaṇī, Buddhist Psychological Ethics, was published in 1974, No. 41 in the Translation Serieṣ These had been preceded by U Nārada’s Discourse on Elements, his translation of Dhātukathā, 1962, reprinted in 1977, and No. 34 in the Translation Serieṣ The demand for these Abhidhamma works, though small, has been steady, and has grown steadily as the years have gone by. There is now a study of the ﬁrst few pages of Paṭṭhāna by U Nārada called Guide to Conditional Relations, Voḷ I. He wished to write it to make explicit and intelligible many of the diﬃculties in the highly complex Paṭṭhāna, the seventh and last of the Abhidhamma workṣ Here again U Nārada’s knowledge is due to the long period of study he has devoted to this work and to the early comprehensive, solid and precise Abhidhamma training he received, a training no longer existing even in Burma. As I said in my Foreword to Conditional Relations, Voḷ I (as it should now be called), it had not been expected that the same translator would translate the Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana vols. II, III, IV, or V. But the unexpected happened and the present book is the resulṭ The preparation of the typescript and of most of the proof-reading
